source.title: Exploiting Adam-like Optimization Algorithms to Improve the Performance of Convolutional Neural Networks
source.authors: L. Nanni; G. Maguolo; A. Lumini

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Compares test accuracy across adaptive optimizers and SGD using ResNet50 on three medical image datasets; it does not measure the train-test gap directly.
record.gate_note: The paper reports optimizer comparisons on natural-label image datasets. It does not test arbitrary-label memorization, width scaling, convolutional versus fully connected architectures, batch size, dropout, sharpness measures, or removal of memorized examples.
record.test_reason: Table 1 directly compares adaptive optimizers with SGD on held-out medical-image classification accuracy, testing V4 in a new setting. All methods use 20 epochs and a global learning rate of 0.001; optimizer-specific tuning is not reported.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors: they describe worse standalone test generalization for Adam methods, average improvements from their variants, and benefits from combining classifiers trained with different optimizers. Their blanket standalone comparison is broader than Table 1 warrants: several BG and LAR variants match or numerically exceed SGD.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a fixed ResNet50 and compares optimizer variants on medical image datasets; the text does not describe limited hyperparameter tuning as the comparison protocol.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported optimizer comparison varies by dataset: HeLa, BG, and LAR show different relative test accuracies.
record.problems: Only one backbone architecture is tested. The paper reports averages and standard deviations over 7 experiments but gives no significance tests. Training accuracy and train-test gaps are not reported.
record.rows_left_out: None; all standalone optimizer results in Table 1 are included. Ensemble results in Table 2 are omitted because the claim version concerns standalone optimizer generalization comparisons.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label versus random-label held-out performance.
Width scaling beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
Training-performance comparisons; learning-rate and schedule tuning; broader tuning; decoupled weight decay; switching from Adam to SGD; language benchmarks.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Removing examples selected by memorization and comparing with random removal.

record.verdict_notes: All Table 1 means and standard deviations are transcribed correctly. Held-out evaluation uses five-fold cross-validation for HeLa and BG and the supplied three-part cross-validation split for LAR. Near-parity states reflect the tiny mean differences relative to reported variability, not a reported equivalence test. No training accuracy or loss is reported, so optimization failure cannot be separated from generalization differences. Table 2 ensembles are already declared omitted and do not isolate the standalone optimizer comparison.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural versus random labels.
Width scaling past the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the effects of local connectivity.
Image-classification optimizer comparisons are reported, but not language benchmarks, broader hyperparameter tuning, decoupled weight decay, switching from Adam to SGD, or word-level language models.
Large-batch comparisons and adaptations to the training recipe.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other measures of the generalization gap.
Removing training examples selected by memorization or influence.

relationships.condition: HeLa; standalone ResNet50, fixed learning rate 0.001 and 20 epochs
relationships.reason: R2–R6 report adaptive-method accuracies of 55.90–79.00%, versus SGD's 92.09% in R1.
relationships.display_finding: The reported higher SGD accuracy than the adaptive methods under the shared fixed learning rate remains unverified.

relationships.condition: BG Adam and Cos#2; LAR Adam, DGrad and Cos#1
relationships.reason: R8, R12, R14, R16 and R17 show only 0.28–1.96-point mean disadvantages versus SGD, with substantial variability and no significance tests.
relationships.display_finding: Selected adaptive methods reportedly trailed SGD amid substantial variability, but these comparisons remain unverified.
